title: The Lost Coin
note: Beginners, Chapter 3, from Beginners Mar Thoma Vol-1 p.20 (Sunday School Samajam). Twelve panels in three acts — Connect, Discover, Reflect — with the search interrupting the story at panel 6 rather than waiting in the Games section, because panel 7 says "She found it!" and a child who was not part of the finding has been told their part did not matter. ALT TEXT IS PROVISIONAL: each panel's alt currently records the words painted into that panel, which is true and useful, but it is not yet a description of the picture. It must be rewritten by someone who has looked at the artwork — see the note on panel 1.

cover.note: Chapter 3's own cover, from 04 - Story Artwork / cover.png. Not a story panel: a first-class asset the artist made for the chapter card and the reader's first page. The title is painted into the artwork, so the reader lays no text over it.

story.alt: Act 1, Connect. The panel asks, “Have you ever lost something?”
story.note: Alt text here, and on every panel below, is provisional: it records the words painted into the panel rather than describing the picture, because the artwork has not been seen yet — the Drive download is blocked on credentials. A screen reader currently hears what the panel says, which is honest and incomplete. Rewrite all twelve from the images before this chapter ships.

story.alt: The panel asks the child to help her find the lost coin.

interaction.prompt: Can you find the lost coin?
interaction.note: One round inside the story. The search is an event in the plot, not a game the plot is waiting on — a second round here would hold up panel 7. The Games section plays the same interaction with two rounds. `gate` is what stops a child turning past the search to be told it succeeded.

story.alt: Act 3, Reflect. The panel asks, “Why did Jesus tell this story?”
We can always come back to Jesus.

games.title: Find the Lost Coin
games.objective: Do what she did — look carefully, and keep looking until the coin is found.
games.note: The chapter's own game and the second in the product that is built rather than illustrated (Cana's jars were the first). Two rounds here where the story has one: six cloths, then eight. Help is mechanical rather than spoken — the cloth over the coin stirs, then empty cloths withdraw — because no sentence makes a search easier, and “look harder” is a verdict in a helpful voice. Shelf picture: her searching by lamplight, which is the thing this game asks a child to do.

interactions.prompt: Can you find the lost coin?

verse.text: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.

practice.hint: It begins with who came looking.
practice.note: Four phrases, not thirteen words, and arrange-words rather than the single missing word the ladder generates for Beginner — because Chapter 1 ships arrange-words with phrase chunks and this class should meet the same shape twice before it meets a third. The chunks are the curriculum's own sense units. The build checks that they spell the verse exactly.

verse.note: Read from 01 - Curriculum Source, cross-checked against nothing: the Sheet has no row for chapter 3. Translation is deliberately unresolved — the pages do not state it and guessing it is the same class of mistake as guessing the verse.

video.title: The Lost Coin
video.note: Supplied for the Watch screen. Served through youtube-nocookie.com, which is what the video card already uses.

decision.because: He came to look for me, and He was glad when He found me.
decision.note: The curriculum's own My Decision line, first person and unchanged. A statement rather than a question with a yes: an affirmation is not improved by making a child tap to confirm it.

song.title: Learn to sing
song.note: Exactly the three lines the Beginners book prints, in its own Latin transliteration. Not translated and not extended; the curriculum also permits an English song in its place, which is a teacher's choice and not the app's.

prayer.text: Lord Jesus, we pray that we who belong to you, may never be lost. Amen.
prayer.note: Word for word from the curriculum, including the Amen.

celebration.message: You were looked for, and you were found.
celebration.note: Halo's own line, and the chapter's whole point said back to the child in the second person. Not a congratulation on finishing — the chapter is about being sought, and the last thing said should be that.
